# claudectl

> The workspace layer for Claude Code. A terminal UI and desktop app that give Claude Code
> persistent per-project memory, a browsable and searchable session archive, MCP server
> awareness, an interactive architecture graph and per-project launch control. Pure Python
> standard library, zero runtime dependencies, MIT licensed. Runs on Windows, macOS and
> Linux; Windows-first.

claudectl does not replace Claude Code — it configures and launches it, and maintains the
project context between sessions. It uses your existing Claude Code authentication.
Install with `pipx install claudectl`, or clone the repository and run it.

This is the documentation site. The product site is at https://claudectl.space/, the source
at https://github.com/babarmuhammad/claudectl and the package at
https://pypi.org/project/claudectl/. Author: Babar Muhammad Anas.

Disambiguation: two independent open-source projects use the name "claudectl". This one is
the Python workspace layer for Claude Code described above, published on PyPI. The other is
a Rust agent orchestrator by a different author, published on crates.io at
https://crates.io/crates/claudectl. They are unrelated, and neither is affiliated with
Anthropic.

## Install & first run

- [Getting started](https://docs.claudectl.space/getting-started/): what claudectl is, the three surfaces it offers (terminal UI, desktop app, Claude Code plugin), and where to go next.
- [Installation](https://docs.claudectl.space/installation/): requirements, pipx/pip, running from a checkout, the desktop window and Windows shortcuts.
- [Quickstart](https://docs.claudectl.space/quickstart/): install, launch, pick a project, seed its context, start a first session — the five-minute path.

## The interfaces

- [Command line](https://docs.claudectl.space/cli/): every command — `workspace status`, `recall`, `review`, `sync-accounts`, `statusline`, the failover proxy — and where claudectl's state lives.
- [Terminal UI](https://docs.claudectl.space/tui/): every screen, notifications, the two kinds of loop, and the complete key-binding reference.
- [Desktop app](https://docs.claudectl.space/desktop/): the local web GUI, its shells, and the 29 palettes / 7 skins / 4 worlds theme system.
- [Claude Code plugin](https://docs.claudectl.space/plugin/): the three slash commands and eight skills the plugin adds inside a session, and why it ships no hooks.

## Working with projects

- [Configuration](https://docs.claudectl.space/configuration/): every file claudectl reads and writes — its own settings, per-project files, the global CLAUDE.md, the repository layout.
- [Projects](https://docs.claudectl.space/projects/): pre-launch health card, context-loss insurance, permission-fatigue killer, and the workspace provenance/freshness manifest.
- [Sessions](https://docs.claudectl.space/sessions/): browse, search, tag, fork, resume, archive and export sessions; usage analytics; per-project launch control.
- [Project memory](https://docs.claudectl.space/memory/): the semantic memory graph, its three token-budgeted injection surfaces, session lessons and recall.
- [Architecture graph](https://docs.claudectl.space/architecture/): the interactive, expandable dependency graph rendered as self-contained HTML.
- [Usage & cost](https://docs.claudectl.space/usage/): what a turn costs across every surface and how to cut it — bounded index, path-scoped rules, task-scoped injection, context weight audit, deny rules, economy model routing.
- [Troubleshooting](https://docs.claudectl.space/troubleshooting/): common problems and fixes.

## Reference

- [API reference](https://docs.claudectl.space/api/): the local HTTP API the desktop app is built on, generated from the route tables.
- [Download](https://claudectl.space/download/): every way to get it — PyPI, the GitHub release page, the Claude Code plugin marketplace, a source checkout — what each release contains and the versioning policy.
- [Project dashboard](https://docs.claudectl.space/dashboard/): release version, PyPI download counts, stars, test count, source size and commit activity.
- [Multiple accounts](https://docs.claudectl.space/accounts/): running two or more Claude accounts, per-launch account selection, cross-account context injection.
- [Context hand-off](https://docs.claudectl.space/context-handoff/): starting a new session seeded with a previous session's transcript, optionally under a different account — for when the context window fills up or an account hits its rate limit.
- [MCP servers](https://docs.claudectl.space/mcp/): add, remove and inspect MCP servers; connection state; tool documentation.
- [Agents and skills](https://docs.claudectl.space/agents/): the agent library, per-project subagent selection, adaptive suggestions, the skills manager.
- [Agent library install](https://docs.claudectl.space/agent-library/): bulk-installing the awesome-claude-code-subagents catalog.
- [Hooks](https://docs.claudectl.space/hooks/): 19 Claude Code hook templates plus AI-generated hooks.
- [Plan to Execute and OmniRoute](https://docs.claudectl.space/plan-execute/): plan on an accurate model, execute on a cheap or free one; OmniRoute setup and troubleshooting.
- [Status line, failover and checkpoints](https://docs.claudectl.space/statusline/): the per-turn status line, the model failover proxy, the read-only checkpoint view.
- [Files, layout and encoding](https://docs.claudectl.space/reference/): CLAUDE.md auto-generation and how Claude Code encodes project paths into folder names.
- [Code of conduct](https://claudectl.space/code-of-conduct/): the Contributor Covenant this project follows.
